land.text: the whole Haitian state, held by the United States as an occupation from 28 July 1915 to 1 August 1934 (infobox) and independent again from 15 August 1934

predecessors.note: Not a real founding: Cliopatria's 'Haiti' (1792-1802), 'Empire of Haiti' (1805-1915) and 'Republic of Haiti' (1936-2024) rows are one continuous state, the republic of 15 January 1859 (infobox 'Republic: 15 January 1859'). The haiti dossier (another part) ends at 1935 and carries the 1915-1934 occupation; this one starts where Cliopatria's third row does.

capitals.name: Port-au-Prince
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Port-au-Prince 18°32′10″N 72°20′47″W'; the page: 'The capital and largest city is Port-au-Prince.' It does not date the seat separately.

keyframe_review.note: 31,292 km2 against the infobox's 27,700 km2 (the body gives 27,750 km2): ratio 1.13, within the factor of two (presumably the grid's coastal margin). The cell set is identical to Cliopatria's Empire of Haiti shape of 1915 and the Dominican Republic's shape does not change in 1935-1937, so the 1936 start is a row boundary and the border treaty of 9 March 1936 moves no cell. La Gonâve is inside the outline; Tortuga, 'located off the coast of northern Haiti', is not (its land cell is left out of the shape), and Navassa Island, 'subject to an ongoing territorial dispute with the United States', has no cell in the grid.
Identical to 1936-2023. The page records no change of frontier after 1936.

region.text: the western third of Hispaniola, the Haitian state of 1936 (identical on the grid to Cliopatria's Empire of Haiti shape of 1915)

ledger.note: 1936: Cliopatria's Republic of Haiti row begins on the land of its earlier Haiti rows; one state, not a founding. The page: 'U.S. forces occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934', the occupation ended 'in 1934, under the Presidency of Sténio Vincent', and the infobox has 'Independence from the United States: 15 August 1934'. Page silent on anything that happened in 1936 itself, so confidence 1.

certainty.note: The only land frontier, with the Dominican Republic, was finally fixed by treaty: 'a final border treaty being signed on 9 March 1936', after the treaty of 27 February 1935 that allocated the disputed sections and the 1929 treaty ('not finally delimited until 1929'). Navassa Island is an undrawn dispute with the United States.

sources.title: Haiti
sources.note: Identity, capital, infobox area 27,700 km2, the 1915-1934 occupation and 15 August 1934, Navassa. Silent on 1936 and on border treaties.

sources.title: Dominican Republic–Haiti border
sources.note: The 1929 treaty, the 27 February 1935 treaty and the final border treaty of 9 March 1936; silent on which sections were disputed and on who gained.

notes: BUDGET: two pages (Haiti; Dominican Republic–Haiti border). ONE STATE, THREE ROWS: see the predecessor note and the haiti dossier; the colour agent should give 'haiti', 'empire-of-haiti' and 'republic-of-haiti' one colour (colours.json carries three). The 1936 'found' is a row boundary at confidence 1. BORDER 1936: the pages date the frontier treaties (1929; 27 February 1935; final treaty 9 March 1936) but name no land and no winner; the Cliopatria shapes do not move, so no gain or loss is recorded here. The dominican-republic dossier (another part) records a 1936 loss of claim to the central border towns (Hinche, Las Caobas, San Miguel de la Atalaya, San Rafael de la Angostura) from a different page; those towns are on the Haitian side of the constant outline. The border page is not read as giving that. NOT OPENED (budget): United States occupation of Haiti (the haiti dossier cites it), the 1937 Parsley massacre (no territorial change), the 2024 gang-held parts of Port-au-Prince (outside the pages read). Rulers omitted: no list page opened. Region names used: Cliopatria shapes only.
